source_note: Every row is one it()/test() scenario present in tests/**/*.test.ts at the frozen head. The count is exactly the suite size reported by that head: 141.

method.KEEP: The scenario's meaning is unchanged by the reset and it returns in the target slice under the same name.
method.REWRITE: The obligation survives but the model it asserted against does not; it returns in the target slice under the stated replacement name.
method.DROP: The scenario tested an artefact of PR #1 that the clean baseline never creates. Permitted only when the named invariants carry the obligation in their own conformance tests.
method.not_a_reason: That a previous review did not object to a scenario is never a reason to KEEP it.
method.added_tests: New conformance tests are declared in invariants.json, never inside this manifest; this manifest describes only the 141 historical scenarios.

rows.scenario: worker report contract > rejects a report with an unknown field
rows.rationale: Strict report parsing survives the reset, but the report shape does not: PR-G's message carries an authenticated principal and a replay token that PR #1's report never had.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: worker report contract > rejects a report missing a required field
rows.rationale: Same obligation, new required set: the fields a report must carry are redefined by PR-G's ingestion contract.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: worker report contract > rejects a report with an unknown status
rows.rationale: The status vocabulary is re-derived from the PR-B state table rather than from PR #1's report enum.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: worker report contract > rejects a report for an unknown task
rows.rationale: Task identity becomes task:<uuid-v4> under the canonical identity rules, so the unknown-task case is re-expressed against that form.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: worker report contract > rejects a report from a worker that does not hold the lease
rows.rationale: Lease possession now distinguishes a reconciliation claim from an execution claim, so 'does not hold the lease' has two distinct failing shapes instead of one.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: worker report contract > records a rejected report so the failure is auditable
rows.rationale: A rejected report must stay auditable; the meaning is unchanged and INV-S6 carries it forward verbatim.
rows.audit_note: Carried forward under the same scenario name.

rows.scenario: coordinator contract > rejects an unknown action
rows.rationale: Coordinator proposals become ingested messages under PR-G's contract, so the unknown-action case moves with them.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: coordinator contract > rejects output with unexpected keys
rows.rationale: Unexpected-key rejection is retained but re-expressed against the versioned canonical serialization rather than an ad-hoc schema.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: coordinator contract > refuses READY_TO_MERGE when no clean verdict exists at the current head
rows.rationale: The premise changed: merge readiness is no longer 'a clean verdict exists at the current head' but 'no unresolved blocking finding on the tuple', with base compared as well as head.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: coordinator contract > refuses REQUEST_REVIEW before CI is green
rows.rationale: CI status becomes an immutable observation recomputed into a current snapshot, so the assertion moves from a stored flag to a recomputed slot.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: coordinator contract > refuses WAIT_DEPENDENCY when nothing is actually blocking
rows.rationale: The dependency graph moves to PR-H and a caller's claim is checked against persisted edges rather than against an in-memory graph object.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: coordinator contract > runs the stub coordinator end to end and records the validation
rows.rationale: The stub coordinator end-to-end walk is rebuilt on the new slices; only its recording obligation is unchanged.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.scenario: coordinator contract > keeps the coordinator advisory: a merge proposal still meets the gate
rows.rationale: The advisory principle survives but the gate it must not bypass is now an APPROVED envelope, not a resolved row.

rows.scenario: phase-0 demo scenario > walks the whole workflow on synthetic data
rows.rationale: The demo is rebuilt over PR-A to PR-H; the scenario's value is that the whole workflow runs on durable state, which is retained.
rows.audit_note: Returns under a new name because the obligation is re-expressed against the reset model.

rows.rationale: Risk labels are now a separate axis from finding severity, so the comparison is re-expressed in risk-label terms and must not borrow severity words.

The obligation it protected — a row that never recorded a decision must not become consent — is INV-R2, which carries its own PR-A negative test, so dropping this row leaves no invariant uncovered.

rows.audit_note: Removed with no replacement; the obligation is covered by the named invariants' own conformance tests.
